xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4835: Phone app: phone credential, pairing exchange and scope rows on the machine

plan.title: Phone app: phone credential, pairing exchange and scope rows on the machine
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The phone app (epic PAN-4823) needs a machine-side identity. Today a secure channel resolves only machine credentials, the link handshake pins only machine keys (server.ts:188), the pairing channel can mint only machine links, and the route-scope table sends pan.getSnapshot, pan.replayEvents and GET /api/activity to admin, so a least-privilege phone credential could neither connect nor boot the phone screens.
narratives.Proposal: Add an access-token kind 'phone' bound to the phone's link key with PHONE_TOKEN_SCOPES (operator machine scopes minus forward); resolve it only inside a link channel from that key; pin its key in the handshake; skip Origin/CSRF for it; mint it through POST /api/phones/exchange on the pairing channel; add DELETE /api/phones/self and PUT /api/phones/self/push-key; list and revoke phones through /api/devices and the Devices panel; report capabilities.phoneApp; add the scope rows the phone surface needs and encode the surface inventory as a test. Full detail, file/line references and before/after code are in .pan/drafts/PAN-4835.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Phone access to linked machines: /api/fleet/needs-you, /api/conversations/@env/... proxying and /ws/linked stay refused to phones (PAN-4887); no change to refuseFleetRequest, chainedHopRefusal or ws-linked.ts
- New scope rows for GET /api/settings, GET /api/color-themes, model-picker reads, push routes or any other admin-only (inventory B) request
- Any phone-side code, the channel HTTP client or shims (W-WEB2, W-APP1), directory or contracts frames (W-CON1/2/3), the QR dialog (W-MAC2) or native push (W-MAC3)
- Trusting capacitor://localhost or any phone origin
- A KIND column in pan devices list, or offline phone revocation in pan devices revoke
- Changes to remote-access/config.ts auto-mint reasons
- User-facing Mintlify pages (configuration/phone-app.mdx and the rest of epic W-DOC)
- Any change to machine, device or token credential behavior
- Counting phones in GET /api/anywhere/status devices.active (it keeps counting browser devices only; the Devices panel lists both)

autoDecisions.summary: Split phone reach to linked machines (fleet Needs-you, @env proxy, /ws/linked) into sibling issue PAN-4887
autoDecisions.rationale: Three no-chained-hops sites refuse every channel caller (D-4651-17); lifting that for phones is a separate security change not named in the issue body and would exceed the 25-file plan budget. This issue meets AC-7 for the paired machine.

autoDecisions.summary: Fix the link-handshake pinning (isPinnedPeer) to accept active phone keys via findActiveChannelTokenByKey
autoDecisions.rationale: Not in the epic's W-MAC1 text, but server.ts:188 refuses any key no machine token pins, so without it the phone never reaches HTTP.

autoDecisions.summary: Add scope rows only when the phone cannot do its core job without them and the response holds no config secret; everything else stays admin
autoDecisions.rationale: Least privilege (epic NFR-4: screens needing other scopes are hidden). Added pending-input (explicit), delete-image (tell, undo of upload-image), activity, getSnapshot, replayEvents and the two self routes.

autoDecisions.summary: Use the static traced inventory of the mobile screens as the WI-6 test fixture instead of the W-APP1 shim log
autoDecisions.rationale: W-APP1 does not exist yet; the traced import closure of MobileApp.tsx is the best available list and W-APP1 can extend it.

autoDecisions.summary: DELETE /api/phones/self closes the caller's own channel like DELETE /api/machines/self; the app treats a dropped response as success
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the existing machine self-revoke pattern and keeps revocation immediate.
Nothing here imports a directory frame type; clientId is a plain UUID v4 string. PAN-4774 (the sequencing gate) is closed.

items.title: Add the phone access-token kind with channel-key lookup

narrative.Action: Follow PRD WI-1 (.pan/drafts/PAN-4835.md). In src/lib/access-tokens.ts add kind 'phone' with phoneKey (64 hex), clientId (UUID v4) and optional pushKey (64 hex) fields; export PHONE_TOKEN_SCOPES (the eight scopes, no admin/forward); extend isRecord so a malformed phone record fails closed and other kinds may not carry phone fields; add the phone branch to createAccessToken refusing admin/forward; add findActiveChannelTokenByKey (machine or phone by key) and setPhonePushKey; document the kind in the header comment. Write tests/unit/lib/access-tokens-phone.test.ts.

items.title: Given a phone token created with phoneKey, clientId and pushKey, when the registry is re-read, then the record returns all three fields and the eight PHONE_TOKEN_SCOPES
createAccessToken rejects a phone token whose scopes include admin or forward, and rejects phoneKey/clientId/pushKey on a device token
Given a registry file holding a phone record without clientId, refreshAccessTokens rejects and verifyAccessToken refuses every token
findActiveChannelTokenByKey returns the active machine record for a machineKey and the active phone record for a phoneKey, and returns null after that record is revoked
setPhonePushKey updates the pushKey of an active phone record and returns null for a revoked one
